correctness.rationale: Soundness and minimality of 3M use singleton-closure forcing. Equality for geodetic graphs is proved by induction on shortest-path distance. In nongeodetic graphs the first ambiguous-distance pair cannot be completed by a one-consequence rule without leaving its selected shortest path. Even-cycle antipodes require hits on both semicircles and a two-output rule achieves exactly four literals; all other rule costs are three. Counting yields the factorial formulas. Direct finite verifier ran successfully for 231 cycle bases and 771 connected labelled graphs; finite testing alone is not the proof. Exact n=3..10 cost list is in VERIFICATION.md.

value.rationale: Optimization of Horn representations is a natural hard problem. Geodesic graph closure provides a canonical finite logic where the global optimum is controlled exactly by a shortest-path uniqueness property, including a converse obstruction. Complete classification and multiplicative enumeration of optimum bases for all geodetic graphs and both parity families of cycles, with a nontrivial antipodal literal penalty, are mathematically motivated structural invariants rather than routine numerical instances. The result does not claim a general nongeodetic algorithm.
